requirements.text: The bidder shall supply, implement, integrate, and support an integrated Hospital Management Information System (HMIS) across four tertiary-care hospitals.

The HMIS shall cover EMR, outpatient and inpatient management, LIS/RIS, pharmacy and inventory management, billing and insurance claims, a central data warehouse with dashboards, and integration with existing hospital systems via HL7/FHIR standards.
The successful bidder shall migrate legacy patient records.
The successful bidder shall train hospital staff.
The successful bidder shall provide three (3) years of post-implementation support and maintenance.
The bidder must be registered with the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) and appear on the Active Taxpayer List.
The bidder must hold a valid ISO 27001 information security management certification.
The bidder must hold a valid CMMI Level 5 appraisal for software development services.
The bidder must have successfully completed at least two (2) health-sector IT system implementations for hospitals or healthcare networks within the last five (5) years.
The assigned project manager must hold a valid PMP certification.
The bidder must submit a bid security of two percent (2%) of the bid price in the form of a bank guarantee or CDR from a scheduled bank.
The HMIS shall support HL7 v2.x and FHIR R4 interoperability for exchange with existing laboratory analyzers and PACS systems.
The bidder must perform structured data migration of legacy patient records with a documented validation and reconciliation methodology.
The system shall provide role-based access control, audit trails, and encryption of patient data at rest and in transit.
The bidder must guarantee system availability of 99.5% measured monthly, with a disaster recovery site and a recovery time objective (RTO) of four (4) hours.
The bidder must deliver structured end-user and administrator training for approximately 1,200 hospital staff across the four sites.
The bidder should provide mobile applications for physicians covering ward rounds, e-prescriptions, and result review.
The bidder must provide a help desk with 24/7 coverage and defined SLAs for incident response during the support period.
Proposals shall be submitted in two separate sealed envelopes marked "Technical Proposal" and "Financial Proposal".
The bid validity period shall be 90 days from the submission deadline.
The bidder must respond to the required proposal sections Q1 to Q5.
The bidder must include in the proposal Q1 covering company profile, registrations, and certifications.
The bidder must include in the proposal Q2 covering relevant project experience with verifiable references.
The bidder must include in the proposal Q3 covering proposed solution architecture and interoperability approach.
The bidder must include in the proposal Q4 covering implementation plan, migration methodology, and training plan.
The bidder must include in the proposal Q5 covering support and maintenance model with SLAs.
